To the public, the framing was simple and completely honest: the President conducting a series of regional working visits to monitor implementation of the Family Readiness Bill, while accompanying the Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy in giving a “Wonderful Indonesia” cultural appreciation award to The Corrs for their dedication in maintaining traditional Irish music roots amid the global music industry for decades — an award specifically realized in the form of a full month cultural journey around Indonesia with the President and her family. No one lied. It's just that not everyone needed to know how much time between those official agendas would be spent hunting durian and getting lost in a floating market.

Several media affiliated with Hardiman Suryo's circle tried to twist it — one editorial titled “Vacation Disguised as an Award?” appeared in the first week. But because the award was genuinely official, the working visit agenda genuinely ran in every province, and The Corrs themselves genuinely deserved that recognition, that attack narrative never found its momentum.

No one asked The Corrs to make anything in return. The album “Nusantara Whispers” born months later came purely from inspiration they found themselves throughout the journey — something never requested, never expected, and therefore felt far more sincere when it finally released and was warmly received by the international music world.

Deirdre in London, hearing this plan from Sharon, at first could only fall silent in shock. But once she confirmed all security and logistics aspects were fully arranged by the Indonesian government — not the label's or band's responsibility at all — she could only say, “You're really going to get a month's vacation, secured by a state, and even given an official award. I just need to say yes.”
But that night, in the still-warm pavilion, everything still felt like a half-formed dream —

And so — the most spontaneous yet most historic decision was born. Not through a cabinet meeting, not through a diplomatic agreement, but through warm laughter and spontaneity on a simple birthday night — which was then tidied up, legitimized, and neatly wrapped as a working visit through three weeks of quiet hard work behind the scenes.
A cross-cultural tour, friendship, and inevitable comic disaster —
which the world would later call with a name full of love:
“Holiday in Indonesia.”
Day 1: “Selamat Maling! Uh, Malam!” — The Corrs' Arrival & Jetlag Attack at the Palace

The next morning after that epic surprise birthday night for President Nisa and the super-sudden month-long vacation decision, the atmosphere in the Palace's private pavilion felt like… well, like there were four international rock stars who had just crash-landed from Dublin and weren't fully aware of where they were.

The Corrs, who technically “never actually left Indonesia” since that surprise concert (because Nisa immediately “secured” them on grounds of “acclimatization before the Nusantara tour”), woke with a combination of leftover jetlag, slight dizziness from too much laughing last night, and disbelief that they were really going to spend a full month in this tropical country with a President.

Andrea was the first to appear in the pavilion dining room, her hair still adorably messy, wearing silk pajamas that probably cost more than a small regency's budget, and reading glasses perched on her nose. Her eyes narrowed seeing Nisa already neat in a casual outfit with a cup of jasmine tea in hand.
“Morning, Andrea! Or… good afternoon Dublin time?” Nisa greeted warmly.

Andrea yawned widely. “Oh, Madam President… Nisa… morning. I think my brain is still left on the plane. This is real, right? We're not dreaming that we're being taken around Indonesia by a President?”
Nisa laughed freely. “Very real, Andrea. And just call me Nisa. Consider me your most VVIP tour guide and also the most… well, probably the busiest.”

One by one, the other Corrs members appeared in similar condition. Sharon, still trying to look elegant though her eyes were puffy from lack of sleep, immediately looked for coffee. Caroline, with her characteristic energy, was already ready with her vlog camera, recording every corner of the pavilion. Jim? As usual, he appeared last, carrying a philosophy book (again!) and immediately asking Reza who had just joined, “Pak Reza, in your opinion, is this concept of jetlag actually a form of the soul's protest against the relativity of space and time?”

Reza, who had already mentally prepared to face Jim's latest conspiracy theory, only smiled patiently. “Maybe we discuss that after breakfast and a bit of rest, Jim. The Palace's special fried rice is waiting.”

Breakfast that day was filled with an introduction to basic Indonesian cuisine that was safe yet still authentic. Fried rice (non-spicy version for Jim and Andrea), chicken porridge (Caroline immediately liked it), and various fresh tropical fruits (Sharon most enthusiastic trying salak, which she thought was a fruit from the dinosaur era because of its skin resembling burnt dragon scales).

After breakfast, the first day's agenda was “Relaxed Briefing and Total Rest.” Nisa, helped by Alex acting as “hip consultant,” tried to briefly explain their month-long travel plan. A giant map of Indonesia was spread on the table, making The Corrs gape at how vast the country they would explore was.
“So, we'll start from Java, Bali, then to Nusa Tenggara, Kalimantan, Sumatra, Maluku… and maybe a little surprise in Raja Ampat if you behave well,” Nisa explained while pointing at spots on the map.
“Wow! That's… so many islands!” Caroline commented in amazement. “Will we take a dragon boat to each island?”
Alex burst out laughing. “No, Auntie. We take the presidential plane, or a pinisi ship if going to small islands. Dragon boats only exist in fairy tales.”

That relaxed briefing was also interspersed with a crash Indonesian language lesson. Nisa tried to teach several basic phrases. “Selamat pagi,” Nisa said. “Suh-la-mat pag-gee,” The Corrs imitated in unison, pretty good. “Selamat siang.” “Suh-la-mat see-yung,” okay, still safe. “Selamat malam.” Well, this is where chaos began. Andrea, full of confidence, bowing slightly formally in the manner of someone greeting an important guest, tried to pronounce, “Selamat… Maling?”

Nisa and Reza immediately exchanged glances, holding back choked laughter with all their might. Alex was already rolling on the sofa. “Not 'Maling,' Andrea,” Nisa corrected in a voice trembling from restrained amusement. “But 'Ma-lam.' Selamat Ma-lam.” “Oh! Ma-lamb! Not Maling! So funny! Got it! So, maling is bad, ma-lam is good!” Andrea exclaimed, feeling she was the smartest.
“Goodness, Jim! We just learned 'selamat malam,' don't jump straight to Robin Hood's moral dilemma,” Sharon cut in while rolling her eyes, which was met with Nisa's laughter.

That first day was indeed dedicated to rest and adaptation. The Corrs spent more time in the pavilion, trying to sleep to overcome jetlag (which turned out harder than imagined because of too much enthusiasm), or simply walking in the Palace's vast garden (with Presidential Security Force escort disguised as gardeners). Andrea even tried “meditating” under a large banyan tree, but five minutes later she was already busy taking selfies with a chubby Palace cat.

That night, during a light dinner, Nisa again tested their Indonesian language ability. “Now, try saying 'selamat malam' correctly,” Nisa asked Andrea. Andrea took a breath, concentrating fully, then said confidently, “Selamat… Maling!” And laughter again exploded in the Palace pavilion's dining room. It seemed this month-long journey would be filled with many unforgettable “Selamat Maling”s.
2: Jakarta's morning sun shone brightly, but for the Corr sibling quartet, the world still felt slightly tilted. The jetlag effect combined with the euphoria of last night's sudden month-long vacation decision made them wake with mixed feelings between adventurous spirit and the desire to pull the thick blanket back over themselves in the super comfortable Palace guest rooms. On this second day, Nisa and Reza deliberately designed a very light schedule, an “Acclimatization Day Full of Question Marks,” where the main focus was relaxation and further introduction to Indonesia's wonders (and oddities) in small doses.

The most anticipated morning agenda (and slightly feared by Andrea) was the Traditional Palace Massage session. After a chicken porridge breakfast that successfully got Caroline addicted (“This is like porridge but a savory version full of fun toppings! Why isn't there porridge like this in Ireland?”) and Jim asked whether the chicken used was organic chicken raised listening to classical music, they were escorted by Reza toward a beautifully carved wooden pavilion in a shady corner of the Palace garden.

Different from luxury spas in five-star hotels, this pavilion radiated an authentic aura of calm. Its floor was made of cool antique tiles, a gentle breeze carried jasmine fragrance from the garden, and the sound of trickling water from a small pond nearby sounded soothing. Four simple yet sturdy wooden massage beds were already neatly arranged, each covered with fine batik cloth. Beside each bed, four middle-aged women with motherly smiles and simple kebaya clothing were waiting. They were the Palace's senior massage therapists, whose fingers reportedly had “magical power” to eliminate all types of aches, from minister-level stress from budget meetings to Presidential Security Force-level stiffness from standing at attention too long.
“This… place is so beautiful,” Sharon whispered to Andrea, admiring the pavilion's atmosphere. “But the therapists look… strong, don't they? Could Andrea be right about the bone-breaking scene?”
Andrea herself had already assumed a wary stance. “I researched last night,” she whispered back. “They say there's a 'crack-crack' massage technique. I don't want a 'crack' sound from my bones!”

Reza, who heard those whispers, only smiled with amusement. “Relax, The Corrs. These ladies are very professional and gentle. This Palace massage is more toward relaxation and improving blood circulation. There's no smackdown scene.”

With slight hesitation (except Caroline who looked most relaxed), they began changing into special batik massage cloths and lying down on their respective beds. The aroma of warm coconut oil mixed with spices like lemongrass and cloves began to be smelled.

The massage session began. The therapists worked in silence, their hands moving steadily, skillfully, and energetically. Caroline, as expected, immediately fell fast asleep within the first ten minutes, her soft snoring becoming an additional soundtrack in that pavilion. Sharon, who indeed liked being massaged, looked to be so enjoying every pressure, occasionally murmuring with pleasure in Irish, making her therapist slightly confused but still smiling.

Jim, the philosopher, initially tried to analyze. He felt pressure at certain points and tried to connect it with the acupressure map he'd once seen in a book. Hmm, this is the kidney meridian point… pressure here should affect the 'chi' water energy in my body… but why do I actually feel a bit sleepy? Roughly that was the content of his complicated head. However, after half an hour, the furrow on his forehead slowly disappeared, replaced by a confused expression between physical enlightenment and philosophical confusion. He looked more relaxed, though his eyes still occasionally opened, observing the pavilion ceiling as if searching for answers there.

Then, there was Andrea. Her massage session was a performance in itself. Every time the therapist's fingers moved to somewhat sensitive areas like the waist or soles of the feet, she would let out a small restrained shriek, then laugh with uncontrollable ticklishness.

“Hihihi! Stop! Stop! Ouch! Tickles! Hahaha!” she squealed repeatedly, making her therapist have to pause briefly while holding back a motherly smile. “That… what was that? Why does it feel like there's a small electric current? Are you using a shock device?” she asked innocently to her therapist, who of course answered with a gentle shake of the head.

Nisa and Reza, being massaged on the other side of the pavilion, could only look at each other and hold back laughter hearing Andrea's chatter. “Seems like Andrea's ticklish nerves are very strategically located, Mas,” Nisa whispered. Reza nodded, “Lucky the therapist is patient. If I were massaging, I might have tickled her until she cried.”

An hour passed so quickly. The massage session ended. The Corrs rose from their beds with varying feelings. Caroline woke with a dazed face and a bit of drool on her cheek. Sharon felt refreshed like after eighteen hours of sleep. Jim felt… physically enlightened but his brain still full of massage theories. And Andrea? She felt ticklish and also extraordinarily relaxed.

“Okay, I have to admit,” she said while stretching her arms. “That was… a very ticklish experience, but also extraordinary! I feel like bread dough that's just been kneaded until smooth! Ready to be baked!”

That afternoon, after lunch and a brief rest, Nisa decided this was the right time to resolve “The Mystery of the Non-Exploding Klepon.” The trauma of klepon exploding in Andrea's mouth the other day seemed to still leave a mark. Nisa wanted to prove that the cute green market snack was actually a friend, not a time bomb.
On the comfortable pavilion terrace, a large plate of still-warm klepon was beautifully served, accompanied by Nisa's favorite jasmine tea. Its fragrance was sweetly tempting.
“Now, here's our star today,” Nisa said while lifting the plate of klepon. “I guarantee, this one has passed the Palace explosion feasibility test.”
Andrea stared at that klepon with a suspicious gaze. “Are you sure, Nisa? Yesterday's explosion was quite powerful, you know. I almost needed a mini fire extinguisher.”
“I'm sure,” Nisa smiled convincingly. “The key is in how you eat it. Remember the lesson? Bite slowly…”
“At the tip first…” Sharon continued, joining in giving instruction.
“Let the palm sugar melt slowly…” Caroline continued.

“…Before finally exploding gracefully inside the oral cavity, producing a taste sensation that is a harmonious blend of palm sugar's rich sweetness, savory grated coconut, and the chewy texture of glutinous rice flour,” Jim concluded, making everyone stare at him strangely. Nisa and Reza looked at each other, then laughed with amusement. “See, Mas. Even klepon he philosophizes,” Nisa whispered.

Andrea took a long breath. “Okay, I'll try again. For Indonesia-Ireland friendship!” She took one klepon with a slightly trembling hand. Stared at it intently. Bit its tip in slow motion. Chewed slowly.
And… no explosion! Only the rich sweetness of palm sugar melting perfectly in her mouth. Her eyes immediately sparkled like a child getting candy.
“SUCCESS! IT DIDN'T EXPLODE! AND THE TASTE… OH MY GOD, THIS IS SO DELICIOUS!” she exclaimed joyfully, immediately grabbing three more klepon without hesitation.

Seeing Andrea's success, the others also attacked the klepon plate. That mystery was finally solved. Klepon could be conquered! This second acclimatization day closed with a sweet victory over a market snack.

That night, they only had a light dinner in the pavilion. Nisa deliberately didn't plan heavy activities, letting The Corrs truly absorb the atmosphere and adapt. There were still many question marks in their minds about Indonesia, about its people's habits, about its food whose names were sometimes scary, but tasted delicious. But at least, today they learned two important things: traditional Palace massage is safe (though ticklish for some people), and klepon can be enjoyed without having to explode. Great progress!
Tomorrow, the real adventure begins. They would fly leaving the Palace comfort zone toward the Island of the Gods, Bali. Ready for morning yoga that might again be disturbed by local fauna?
3: The journey from Jakarta's hustle toward Ubud felt like entering another dimension. The presidential plane landed gracefully at Ngurah Rai Airport, and as soon as the door opened, Bali's warm humid air, laden with the aroma of incense and frangipani flowers, immediately welcomed them. Different from the more formal first welcome in Jakarta, this time the atmosphere was far more relaxed. Nisa had deliberately requested no excessive ceremony. Only several local officials welcomed them briefly with friendly smiles and fragrant frangipani flower garlands that immediately made Andrea sneeze (again!).

The land journey to Ubud took about an hour and a half, passing roads that grew increasingly narrow, winding among traditional villages, art galleries, and expanses of green rice fields beginning to dominate the view. The private villa Nisa and Reza chose was located somewhat remotely, at the end of a small road only one car wide, promising absolute tranquility and privacy. The building was a blend of modern Balinese architecture with natural touches of wood and stone, surrounded by a lush tropical garden and an infinity pool that seemed to merge with the green valley before it.
“This place… is like a postcard come to life!” Sharon exclaimed as she stepped into the villa's open lobby area, her eyes widening in amazement at the view. “Insane, these vibes!”
“Better than a postcard!” Caroline chimed in, already taking out her phone again. “My vlog and Instagram are going to explode today!”

Jim, meanwhile, was already immersed in observing the wood carving details on one of the pillars. “This dragon carving… does it symbolize this villa's spiritual guardian, or is it merely an aesthetic ornament?” he asked one of the villa staff who happened to pass, who could only grin in confusion.

After a smooth check-in and a welcome drink of fresh soursop juice (which made Andrea ask whether this was a real fruit or the result of genetic engineering because of its strange shape), Nisa announced their first agenda in Ubud.

“Alright, my beloved Irish rock stars,” Nisa began with a meaningful smile, “after quite an exhausting journey, it's time we align our energy with Ubud's peaceful nature. Let's begin our first day here with… Morning Yoga!”

On the villa's very spacious back terrace, facing directly onto the spectacular terraced rice field view and Mount Agung faintly visible in the distance, yoga mats were already neatly arranged. Ibu Wayan, the petite yoga instructor with a smile as bright as sunshine who yesterday had (half) succeeded in calming The Corrs during the failed-focus meditation at the Palace, was present again. This time she looked more mentally prepared to face her unique VVIP “students.”

“Good morning everyone,” Ibu Wayan greeted gently, her voice like a soothing melody. “Today we will try several basic Hatha Yoga poses, focusing on breathing and gentle stretching. Let us release all tension, breathe in Ubud's fresh air, and let ourselves merge with nature.”

Nisa and Reza, who indeed did yoga routinely, immediately took position with fluidity. Alex, who was coaxed into joining with the lure of a delicious smoothie bowl afterward, tried to follow with a slightly lazy teenage style but still made an effort. Sharon looked serious and tried to imitate Ibu Wayan's movements with a musician's precision.

But not the others. Andrea, wearing a bright pink branded yoga outfit (very contrasting with the rice fields' green), was busier ensuring her appearance stayed on point in every pose. Is this angle good for photos later? Is my hair messy? Ugh, does this pose make my stomach look bloated? she thought inwardly.

Jim, trying the Trikonasana (triangle) pose, instead looked like he was trying to solve a complex geometry formula with his body. His long legs looked stiff, his hands trembled, and his expression was full of thinking concentration. If my leg angle is 45 degrees and my hand forms a straight line upward, does this mathematically create perfect balance, or is it only an optical illusion? Never mind yoga, Jim was busy calculating Pythagoras in his head.

Caroline, who fundamentally couldn't stay still, looked most restless. During Savasana pose (corpse pose) at the end of the initial stretching session, where everyone was supposed to relax lying still, she instead began tapping her fingers on the mat following her own heartbeat rhythm. Thump thump tap thump… if the tempo were sped up a bit, this could be a cool rock song intro…
“Mbak Caroline,” Ibu Wayan admonished gently without opening her eyes. “Empty your mind, focus on your breath…”
“Oh, yes, Bu Wayan, sorry,” Caroline murmured, trying to stay still, but her feet began making small movements.

When they began trying the Adho Mukha Svanasana pose (Downward-Facing Dog), this is where the second incident involving local fauna occurred. Andrea, who was struggling hard to hold in her stomach so it would look flat in that bent-over pose, suddenly felt something moving at the edge of her yoga mat. Something green. Something with long antennae and spiny legs.
“NOOOOO! IT'S BACK! DON'T COME NEAR ME!”

Andrea's shrill scream shattered Ubud's morning silence. She immediately leaped up, pointing hysterically toward her mat. There, casually, a bright green praying mantis was doing a pose resembling Upward-Facing Dog, as if mocking Andrea's yoga efforts.
“Kung fu grasshopper! It came for revenge because I chased it away yesterday!” Andrea exclaimed in panic, running to seek protection behind Reza this time.
Nisa couldn't hold back her laughter while shaking her head. “Andrea, that might be a different grasshopper! There are so many grasshoppers here.”
“Same thing! They must be one gang!” Andrea retorted, her eyes warily observing the grasshopper still perched casually.

Ibu Wayan again smiled with full Zen patience. She walked closer, gently took a leaf, and moved that grasshopper to an ornamental plant in the nearest pot. “He only wanted to join in seeking enlightenment this morning, Mbak Andrea,” she said calmly. “He is nature's friend, the same as us.”
“A nature friend with such a judgmental stare? What a know-it-all grasshopper!” Andrea murmured, still not fully convinced.

After the grasshopper drama was successfully calmed (though Andrea still occasionally glanced warily toward the plant pot), the session continued with brief meditation. They sat cross-legged facing the extraordinarily beautiful rice field view.
“Now, let us close our eyes,” Ibu Wayan instructed again. “Listen to nature's sounds around us. The sound of wind, the sound of water, the sound of birds… Let our minds be calm, flowing like water…”
Silence. Nature's sounds were indeed melodious. Nisa tried to focus on her breath, feeling calm beginning to envelop her. Reza looked devout. Sharon looked peaceful. But then…
Zeeeee… Bzzzzt…

A loud buzzing sound was heard approaching. A honeybee (or maybe a wasp, no one dared confirm) flew circling above Jim's head. Jim, whose eyes were closed, initially tried to ignore it, considering it part of “nature's sounds.” But that buzzing grew closer, increasingly disturbing his philosophical concentration.

Is this buzzing the universe's frequency trying to communicate, or merely an insect trapped in its mortal life cycle? Jim's mind churned. Finally, he couldn't take it. “Ah, enough already!” He opened his eyes, waving his hand slowly trying to shoo the bee.

On the other side, Caroline who was trying to empty her mind was instead distracted by the aroma of cooking beginning to be smelled from the villa kitchen. Hmm, what smell is that? Smells like fried shallots… will lunch be fried rice again? Ugh, now I'm hungry… Her stomach sounded again, gurgle gurgle, this time louder than yesterday.

Andrea? Don't ask. Every time there was a rustle of leaves or flap of bird wings, she immediately opened her eyes slightly, ensuring it wasn't the kung fu grasshopper gang coming to attack. Her meditation was more like a Presidential Security Force high-level alertness drill.
Ibu Wayan, feeling the “failure-to-focus” energy so strong from her students, finally ended the meditation session earlier than planned.
“It's alright,” she said with an understanding smile. “Finding tranquility takes practice. What matters is we've tried opening ourselves to nature this morning.”
Nisa approached Ibu Wayan. “Thank you so much, Bu Wayan. Forgive my 'students' who are slightly… too full of energy.”

Ibu Wayan laughed a little. “You're welcome, Madam President. It was actually very unique. I've never taught yoga for Irish rock stars who scream hysterically afraid of grasshoppers and have a philosopher friend who likes asking about aliens.”

The third day in Ubud indeed didn't fully go according to Nisa's relaxation plan. But at least, they all got a yoga and meditation experience that was… very memorable. And maybe, a little lesson about accepting imperfection (and the presence of grasshoppers) in life. Tomorrow, an art challenge awaits. Would their work be more “successful” than this morning's yoga session? Nisa could only hope (and pray).
4: The fourth morning in Ubud began with the aroma of freshly brewed Bali coffee and nature's sounds that (this time) sounded truly soothing, without added sound effects from Caroline's growling stomach or the buzzing bee disturbing Jim's meditation. After a colorful smoothie bowl breakfast (which again made Jim ask about the artistic significance of dragon fruit and chia seed arrangement), Nisa announced that day's cultural agenda.
“Since yesterday our yoga session was… ahem… a bit full of distractions,” Nisa began with an amused smile, “today we'll try something calmer with no grasshoppers: learning to make Canang Sari.”

Ibu Wayan, the multitalented yoga instructor whose patience was as thin as silk thread yet as strong as steel, was present again at the villa pavilion. This time, instead of yoga mats, that pavilion was filled with baskets containing fresh green young coconut leaves, various brightly colored flowers (white frangipani, yellow jepun, pink roses, purple balsam), pieces of fragrant pandan leaves, and other accompaniments like candy, small biscuits, even a clove cigarette (which made Andrea immediately ask whether this was an offering for the smoking god).

“This Canang Sari is a form of devotion, our daily gratitude to Ida Sang Hyang Widhi Wasa for life's blessings,” Ibu Wayan explained in her gentle voice, while beginning to demonstrate how to fold young coconut leaves into a small box-shaped canang container called ceper. Her hands moved so fluidly and quickly, as if dancing. “Every element and direction of placement has deep philosophical meaning.”
She explained the meaning of flower colors representing cardinal directions and certain deities.

“Wow, it's quite complicated,” Caroline commented while trying to imitate Ibu Wayan's leaf folding, but the result more resembled a failed ketupat. “This is like origami but a more fragrant version that makes you hungry looking at the candy.”

Nisa and Reza, already fairly familiar with canang, tried helping the other Corrs. Sharon, with a musician's meticulousness, succeeded in making a fairly neat ceper. She arranged her flowers with a beautiful color gradation. “This is like arranging a harmony composition, but with flowers,” she said with a satisfied smile.

Jim, of course, had a different approach. He didn't immediately arrange, but instead asked Ibu Wayan a barrage of questions. “Bu Wayan, if white flowers symbolize Iswara's purity in the east, and red symbolizes Brahma's courage in the south, then what if I want to symbolize… the existential confusion of a jetlagged Irish musician in the middle of a tropical island? What color is suitable?” Ibu Wayan could only smile while answering diplomatically, “Oh dear, maybe you could just use mixed flowers, Bapak Jim.”

Then came Andrea's turn. She observed carefully the example canang Ibu Wayan made, then her eyes roamed looking at the available materials. Besides flowers, there were also small pieces of sugarcane, several marie regal biscuits, and ginger candy. A “brilliant” idea appeared in her head.

She made her ceper (with a little help from Nisa because her leaves kept tearing), then began arranging its contents. Flowers she arranged in a circle at the edge like a pizza crust. In the middle, instead of porosan and mixed flowers, she placed marie regal biscuits as the “dough base,” then sprinkled ginger candy crumbs as “seasoning,” and finally, stuck several small pieces of sugarcane as “pepperoni topping.”
“Voila!” she exclaimed proudly while lifting her work. “A special offering from Andrea Corr: Canang Sari Pizza Funghi Biskoti! How is it? Eye-catching, right?!”

Nisa and Reza immediately burst out laughing seeing Andrea's “masterpiece.” Alex who had just arrived immediately photographed it. Sharon could only shake her head seeing her sister's behavior. Jim approached, observing that pizza canang with a furrowed brow. “Visually compositionally, this is interesting. Combining sacred and profane elements in one container. A post-modern critique of ritualism, perhaps?”

Ibu Wayan approached, staring at that Mini Pizza Canang with an expression of… resigned smile. “Mbak Andrea,” she said as softly as possible, “this is very… creative. But maybe… the biscuit and sugarcane topping could be saved for a snack later?”
“Oh, so toppings aren't allowed?” Andrea asked, disappointed. “And I thought the gods also liked snacking.”

That canang-making learning session ended with varied results. Sharon's canang was neatest, Nisa and Reza's canang standard but full of meaning, Alex's canang simple but decent, Caroline's canang somewhat dented but full of spirit, Jim's canang full of philosophical questions, and Andrea's canang… well, ready to be patented as a new menu item at an Ubud hipster cafe.

After the “canang art crisis” and a lunch break filled with Balinese mixed rice (Jim asked whether 'mixed' here meant mixed with Ubud's mystical energy), the afternoon agenda was a free painting session in the villa garden. Nisa thought, maybe with canvas and paint media, The Corrs' artistic expression could be more… directed?
Canvases of various sizes and colorful acrylic paint sets were already prepared under the shelter of a frangipani tree. The theme was free: “Express Your Feelings About Bali.”

Nisa returned to her impressionist style, painting the silhouette of Uluwatu Temple at sunset with gentle brush strokes. Reza, after failing to paint Nisa yesterday, this time chose an easier object: painting a chubby cat sleeping in a rattan chair. Alex, still with his metal soul, painted a Balinese barong but with a metal band artwork style touch.

Sharon, with full feeling, painted a rice field landscape with her violin floating in the sky, as if playing a melody for the rice goddesses. Caroline, forgetting form and line for a moment, painted an explosion of bright colors — red, yellow, green, blue — which she said was “the visualization of gamelan sounds that make my heart party!”

And Jim? Like when making canang, he brooded a long time before his white canvas. The others had nearly finished painting, Jim's canvas was still completely empty. Then, suddenly he grabbed a brush, dipped it in black, silver, and a bit of dark blue paint, and began stroking with quick, random, yet seemingly full-of-calculation movements. Straight lines crossing each other, concentric circles, strange symbols resembling a mixture between Egyptian hieroglyphs and electronic circuit diagrams.
After about half an hour, he set down his brush. His painting was finished. Totally abstract, geometric, cold, and… confusing.
“Jim, this is… very… interesting,” Nisa commented carefully, trying to understand the artwork before her. “Goodness, may we know what inspired it?”

Jim stared at his painting, then stared at Nisa and the others with the gaze of a scientist who had just discovered a new theory. “This,” he began in a serious tone, “is a map of the star constellations visible from the southern hemisphere at the time the Atlantis civilization is presumed to have reached its technological peak, projected into the ley lines energy field centered in Ubud, and showing the possible landing point location of ancient alien spacecraft that may have been the ancestors of the gods in Balinese and Irish mythology.”
Silence.
Andrea broke the silence by whispering to Caroline, “See! What did I tell you! He must have drunk too much nutmeg juice yesterday.”

Reza, this time truly at a loss for words, could only pat Jim's shoulder while murmuring, “Extra… extraordinary, Jim. This… this isn't just a painting. This is an intergalactic doctoral thesis! We must send it to NASA immediately!”
Alex hurriedly photographed Jim's painting. “This will be The Corrs' next album cover art — the coolest and also the most confusing in the world!”

The “Art Crisis in Bali” that day truly reached its peak. From pizza-shaped Canang Sari to an alien treasure map painting, Ubud had witnessed The Corrs' wildest and most unexpected artist side. Nisa could only hope that their artistic souls would be a bit more “normal” when they tried to enjoy Bromo's natural beauty tomorrow. At least, on a volcano, there's no canang or canvas, right? (Or maybe Jim would find inspiration in the crater smoke patterns?)

That night closed with a delicious Bebek Betutu dinner (Jim asked whether this betutu seasoning used a secret Atlantis recipe) and a session sharing stories about their artwork. They all agreed that although the results might be somewhat… beyond reason, the process of creating together itself was very enjoyable and refreshing. Art doesn't always have to be beautiful or easy to understand; sometimes what matters is the laughter and togetherness behind it.
5: The fifth day in Ubud's tropical paradise began with a deliberately slowed tempo. After the first four days full of adaptation, culture shock, art crisis, and slight grasshopper trauma, Nisa and Reza decided that today was the day of “Total Relaxation Without Question Marks (Hopefully!).” The main agenda? A Balinese-style spa day at their own villa, complete with professional therapists and traditional concoctions promising tranquility of soul and body.

The morning began with a relaxed breakfast on the terrace, accompanied by the trickling sound of water from the koi pond and rice field views still blanketed in thin mist. This time there was no morning yoga schedule inviting the presence of kung fu grasshoppers. Instead, after breakfast, the pavilion area used yesterday for learning canang was now transformed into a mini spa paradise. Several massage beds had been rearranged, decorated with fresh frangipani flowers, and the aroma of essential oil mixed with lemongrass, sandalwood, and ylang-ylang wafted gently, creating a truly peaceful atmosphere. Three Balinese female therapists with serene smiles and simple traditional clothing were ready to welcome their VVIP “patients.”

“Okay, friends,” Nisa announced with a wide smile. “Today we'll pamper ourselves. Forget for a moment about packed schedules, philosophical questions, or glasses-stealing monkeys. Today is Balinese-style me-time! Please take note, vlogger!”

The Corrs looked enthusiastic, though there was slight hesitation in Andrea's eyes. “There… won't be any more strange rituals, right, Nisa? Like the flower bath whose flowers might have caterpillars in them like yesterday?”

Nisa laughed. “Relax, An. Today is pure relaxation. There's Balinese massage, traditional spice scrub, and maybe this afternoon soaking in warm water with flowers again, but I guarantee this time the flowers have passed Palace pest inspection!”

The spa session began with Balinese massage. Different from the Palace massage that focused more on muscles and inner strength, this Balinese massage felt gentler, flowing, using lots of warm coconut oil and rhythmic thumb and palm pressure. Caroline, who yesterday was still slightly tense from nearly becoming an Irish flag after forgetting sunblock, now completely surrendered and returned to soft snoring within the first fifteen minutes. Sharon, the true massage connoisseur, looked to be so enjoying it that occasionally a sigh of pleasure was heard that made her therapist smile.

Jim, this time didn't ask much. He looked to be genuinely trying to relax, closing his eyes, though occasionally Nisa saw his eyebrows furrow, perhaps trying to crack the code behind the massage pressure at his body's meridian points. (A true philosopher never really takes a holiday.)

And Andrea? After yesterday's ticklishness incident, this time she looked more prepared. She tried to focus on her breathing, enjoying the oil's warmth and aromatherapy. Occasionally she still flinched when the therapist pressed certain points, but this time there were more sighs of relief than ticklish shrieks. “Okay, this… this is much better than the 'bone-breaking' massage I imagined!” she murmured to her therapist, who only smiled understandingly.

Nisa and Reza themselves chose to be massaged side by side in a slightly more private corner of the pavilion. For Nisa, moments like this were a rare luxury. Releasing for a moment the burden of state responsibility, letting her muscles stiff from too much sitting in meetings or standing at official events become relaxed. She glanced at Reza beside her, who looked so peaceful with closed eyes. Moments like this, comfortable silence together, felt more valuable than any speech of praise.

After the massage session that made bodies feel light as cotton, it was time for the main attraction: Traditional Spice Scrub. The therapists brought bowls containing thick brownish-yellow paste whose aroma was… unique. A mixture of turmeric, rice-kencur, ginger, cinnamon, and who knows what other secret spices.
“What's this for?” Caroline asked suspiciously, pointing at the scrub bowl with her chin.
“This is lulur, Mbak Caroline,” one therapist explained. “To lift dead skin cells, smooth, and brighten the skin. The beauty secret of Javanese and Balinese palace princesses in the old days.”
“Oh, so after this I can become a palace princess?” Caroline asked innocently, making Alex who happened to be passing by carrying cold drinks cough holding back laughter.

The scrubbing procession began. Their bodies were coated with that warm spice paste, then rubbed slowly to lift grime and dead skin cells. At first it felt a bit strange, like being coated with rendang seasoning but a cold version. But over time, the warm sensation from the spices began feeling comfortable.
However, a problem arose with Andrea. Her sensitive nose turned out to react to one of the fairly strong spice aromas, perhaps the cinnamon powder or the ginger.
“Hah… hah… ACHOOO! Goodness!”

A loud sneeze suddenly shattered the spa's silence. Not just once, but repeatedly. Every time the therapist tried to continue the scrubbing process on her chest area, Andrea would sneeze again dramatically.
“Goodness! Bless you! Bless you!” Sharon said from the next bed, trying to hold back laughter.
“I… ACHOO!… don't know… ACHOO!… why!” Andrea exclaimed between her sneezes, her eyes beginning to water. “Oh dear! It seems… ACHOO!… I'm allergic to being a palace princess!”

Her therapist promptly cleaned Andrea's chest area and tried to avoid the area near her nose. But still, every time that scrub aroma wafted, Andrea's nose reacted again. Andrea's scrubbing session ended earlier than the others, with a bright red nose and watery eyes, but her skin did feel smoother (after successfully stopping the sneezing).
“Okay, note to self: Indonesian spices are delicious to eat, but dangerous if inhaled too closely,” Andrea murmured while drinking the warm ginger tea Reza offered to relieve her sneezing.

After the scrub session finished and bodies were rinsed clean, the event continued with relaxed soaking in the Jacuzzi or the villa pool, which this time had been sprinkled with fresh flowers (which Nisa had made sure were caterpillar-free). Warm water and rice field views now brightly lit by afternoon sun felt so perfect.

Nisa, Reza, Sharon, and Jim looked to be enjoying this calm moment. But not Caroline and Andrea. Somehow, their energy seemed to have returned fully after the massage and scrub (full of sneezing drama). They were instead busy playing in the water like children, splashing each other and laughing out loud, making the previously zen atmosphere a bit more… boisterous.
“Caroline! Andrea! Oh dear, please! Remember your age!” Sharon admonished half-jokingly, which was only answered by a water splash from her sister.

Toward dusk, as the sun began descending and the sky changed color to golden orange, Nisa invited The Corrs to sit relaxed in the bale bengong (Balinese-style gazebo) at the pool's edge. Warm tea and hot fried bananas were served. The atmosphere was so peaceful, so magical.

That's when the second “surprise” of the day appeared. Not a grasshopper, not sneezing. But thousands of small points of light beginning to twinkle among the trees and rice fields before them. Fireflies!
“Oh my God! Look at that!” Caroline shrieked in amazement, pointing toward those twinkling lights. “Amazing! Stars falling to earth!”
Andrea was also enchanted. “So beautiful! This is like a fairy tale land!”
Nisa smiled seeing their reaction. “Those are fireflies, friends. Night insects that can emit light.”

But Jim, with his always-active skeptical soul, narrowed his eyes. “Are we sure those are biological insects, Nisa? The form of their luminescence, their blinking intervals… the pattern is too regular. Could it be…” he brought his face closer, whispering dramatically, “…those are micro surveillance drones sent by foreign intelligence to spy on us? Spy fireflies!”

Everyone fell silent a moment, digesting Jim's conspiracy theory. Then, Nisa, Reza, Alex, Sharon, and Caroline simultaneously burst out laughing. Even several Presidential Security Force members guarding somewhat farther away smiled with amusement hearing that theory.
“Jim, oh Jim,” Sharon said while wiping away tears from laughing. “Goodness, sometimes I think your imagination is our band's greatest asset, and also our greatest source of headache.”
Jim only shrugged. “A philosopher must always question reality, mustn't he?”

That Spa Day Full of Surprises finally ended with full stomachs from fried bananas, smooth skin from the scrub (minus Andrea who was slightly traumatized by the spice aroma), relaxed muscles from the massage, and heads full of spy firefly conspiracy theories from Jim Corr.

Nisa felt that day, though there was a bit of sneezing drama and strange theories, was a very much needed day. A moment to truly release exhaustion, laugh at silly things, and enjoy the simple beauty Bali offered. Their bond of friendship felt increasingly warm, increasingly fluid. And Nisa knew, the positive energy from this relaxation day would become important provision for facing the next adventure (and silliness) in Bromo.
6: Day 6: “Misty Bromo, Hot Chocolate, and Jim's Volcanic Dust Theory” — A Shivering Cold Sunrise

Parting with Ubud's warmth and greenery felt slightly melancholic, even for The Corrs who had only been there a few days. However, the promise of a new adventure at a legendary active volcano in East Java was enough to reawaken enthusiasm (and slight nervousness, especially for Caroline who imagined hot lava). The short flight from Denpasar to Surabaya or Malang (Nisa chose the safest and most comfortable route, of course, with a little help from presidential facilities) went smoothly, though Jim did ask a flight attendant whether the light turbulence earlier was caused by minor tectonic plate shifting or just ordinary wind.

The land journey from the airport toward the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park area became a dramatic transition. The landscape slowly changed from busy lowlands to winding green hills, then climbed increasingly higher entering the Tengger mountain area whose air felt increasingly piercingly cool. The villa or hotel where they stayed was located at altitude, offering an initial view of the vast Tengger caldera stretching out, a sight that made The Corrs gape momentarily in amazement.

“This… this is like a landscape painting in a Lord of the Rings film, but real!” Sharon exclaimed, her eyes not leaving their room window facing directly onto the sand sea expanse and mountain silhouettes in the distance.

Dinner that day was filled with warm mountain specialty dishes — oxtail soup, grilled corn, and ginger tea. Nisa and Reza gave a brief briefing about the next morning's 'super important' agenda: hunting the sunrise at Penanjakan Peak, the highest viewpoint to witness the sunrise moment with Mount Bromo, Mount Batok, and the mighty Mount Semeru as backdrop.
“Okay, listen carefully,” Nisa said in a serious but still friendly tone. “We'll depart at… three in the morning.”

“THREE AM?!” Andrea, Caroline, and Sharon chorused simultaneously, their eyes widening in horror. “Insane! In Ireland at that hour the party is just ending!” Caroline exclaimed. Only Jim looked calm, perhaps contemplating the concept of dawn in different time zones.

“Yes, three in the morning,” Nisa nodded. “And up there it will be extremely cold. Very cold. So, wear all the warm clothes you brought. Three layers, four layers if needed. Scarf, beanie, gloves, thick socks, everything!”
“How cold exactly, Nisa?” Andrea asked, imagining Dublin's winter cold.
Reza smiled mischievously. “Just think of it like you're entering a giant freezer while riding a trail motorcycle, Andrea. Roughly like that.”

Reza's description successfully made Andrea (and Caroline) slightly pale. That night, they all slept early, though enthusiasm mixed with anxiety made sleep not too sound. Andrea even dreamed of being chased by a giant snowman in a sand desert.

And sure enough, the 2:30 AM alarm felt like the world's cruelest torture. Cold air immediately pierced as soon as they emerged from the blanket's warmth. With eyes still half closed and robot-like movements from wearing layered clothing (Caroline even wore two beanies at once), they were escorted toward the fleet of 4x4 Jeeps already waiting.

The journey toward Penanjakan Peak in pre-dawn darkness was an adventure in itself. Narrow roads, steep climbs, and sharp turns made hearts pound. Andrea closed her eyes the whole way while reciting prayers in Irish. Caroline gripped Alex's arm tightly. Sharon tried to enjoy the twinkling village lights below slowly receding, while Jim… he was busy asking the Jeep driver about the engine specifications and suspension system of that tough vehicle. Nisa and Reza could only exchange glances in a separate Jeep, hoping everything would go smoothly.

Arriving at the Penanjakan parking area, the temperature felt increasingly biting. Dozens of other Jeeps were already parked, and hundreds of people (local and international tourists) already packed the viewpoint area, all awaiting the same golden moment. With help from the Presidential Security Force who promptly cleared a path (and perhaps slightly shooed away street vendors too aggressively offering extra beanies to Andrea), this VVIP group got the best position at the edge of the barrier fence.

The sky was still pitch dark, decorated only by scattered stars that looked so close and bright at this altitude. The cold air made their breath look like white smoke. Everyone waited in silence full of anticipation.

Then, slowly but surely, the miracle began. A thin reddish-orange line began appearing on the eastern horizon, chasing away the thick darkness. That color slowly spread, changing to orange, then pink, then golden, painting the sky with a color gradation so beautiful it was hard to express in words.

And when the sun finally truly peeked shyly from behind the mountain's back, its golden light began illuminating the landscape below them. Thick mist that had earlier blanketed the caldera slowly parted, revealing the most iconic view in East Java: the vast sand sea stretching out, Mount Batok perfectly cone-shaped with its characteristic lines, and of course, Mount Bromo standing mighty with thin smoke puffing from its crater. In the distance, Mahameru peak (Mount Semeru), Java's highest mountain, stood towering gracefully, sometimes spewing its own smoke as a morning greeting.
“Oh… my God…” Andrea whispered, her eyes glistening, truly hypnotized by the view before her. The cold that earlier pierced her bones seemed forgotten.
Sharon could only shake her head in disbelief, an amazed smile never leaving her lips. Caroline had already forgotten her vlog camera; she just stood frozen, enjoying that moment wholeheartedly.
Even Jim, the skeptical philosopher, looked silent longer than usual, his eyes fixed toward Bromo's crater puffing smoke.

Nisa put her arm around Reza's shoulder, resting her head. “It always manages to give me goosebumps, this view, doesn't it, Mas,” she whispered. Reza nodded, returning his wife's embrace. Moments like this reminded them of nature's greatness and how small Palace political drama is compared to the majesty of God's creation.

After the sun had risen high enough and the crowd began thinning slightly, it was time for the second best part after sunrise: Hot Chocolate! At one simple stall near the viewing area, they all ordered that warm drink. Steaming tin glasses of thick hot chocolate were served along with warm fried bananas freshly lifted from the pan.
“AAAAH! THIS IS MY LIFESAVER!” Andrea exclaimed after sipping her hot chocolate. The warmth spreading in her throat and stomach felt like an embrace from within.
“This is the most delicious chocolate I've ever drunk! Must try!” Caroline chimed in agreement, her lips smeared with chocolate.
They enjoyed that warm drink and fried bananas while continuing to gaze at the Bromo landscape now brightly lit. The atmosphere became more relaxed, laughter began being heard again.
That's when Jim, after finishing his hot chocolate in silence while continuing to stare toward the sand sea, finally spoke up.
“Nisa, Reza,” he called seriously. “I was observing the volcanic dust particles flying around when we were at the fence edge. Very fine, almost invisible, but everywhere.”
Nisa and Reza exchanged glances, smiling with resignation. Already guessing where this was heading.

“According to my hypothesis,” Jim continued, his eyes now shining full of theoretical enthusiasm, “this volcanic dust isn't merely ordinary eruption residue. I suspect these microscopic silica particles actually function as… a giant natural hard drive!”
“Hard drive? What do you mean, Om Jim?” Nisa repeated in confusion.

“Yes! Just imagine,” Jim began theorizing, his hands moving explaining. “Every major eruption in the past didn't only spew volcanic material, but also recorded the earth's 'memory' at that time — magnetic fields, atmospheric composition, even perhaps energy vibrations from cosmic events — into the crystal structure of this dust! So, the sand sea down there isn't merely sand, but an immensely vast library of geological and cosmic history!”

He stared at Nisa and Reza with a meaningful gaze. “If we could find a way to 'read' the data stored in this volcanic dust, we might be able to uncover the universe's secrets! Maybe this has something to do with the inter-dimensional portal at Borobudur I theorized yesterday!”
Andrea, Sharon, Caroline, Alex, Reza, and Nisa could only fall silent, trying to process “Jim's Volcanic Dust Theory” that had just been launched at 2,700 meters above sea level.

Finally, Alex was the first to break the silence. “Om Jim, that theory is so cool! But if the dust is a hard drive, that means we just drank hot chocolate that might have a 'file' recording an ancient massive eruption?”
Jim nodded seriously. “Very possible, Alex. That adds another interesting dimension to our culinary experience this morning.”
Andrea immediately set down her half-finished hot chocolate glass. “What?! Wait a second! So I just drank… an ancient eruption file?!”

And laughter again exploded in that small stall, louder than before. That shiveringly cold Bromo sunrise finally closed with the warmth of hot chocolate, fried bananas, and of course, the most absurd geological-cosmic conspiracy theory from Jim Corr. The adventure in Bromo wasn't over yet, because after this they would descend to the sand sea. Roughly, what other theory would emerge from Jim when facing Bromo's crater directly?
7: Parting with Malang's cool air and memories of Rawon Setan (which still made Andrea shudder slightly when she remembered its name) felt sweet yet full of anticipation. Next destination: Lombok! The exotic island in West Nusa Tenggara promising white sand beaches, blue-green seawater, and of course, new culinary challenges ready to test The Corrs' tongues (and patience).

The flight to Lombok Praya International Airport went smoothly. This time, Jim didn't ask too much about aircraft engines; it seemed he was still busy contemplating the mystery of Bromo's volcanic dust. Andrea was more prepared with an eye mask and calming music playlist to anticipate turbulence (which turned out not to happen). Sharon was engrossed reading a book about Sasak culture Nisa lent her, while Caroline was busy editing yesterday's apple-eating contest video to upload to her private Instagram account.

Upon landing in Lombok, the difference in atmosphere was immediately felt. The air was warmer, drier, with a faint sea aroma. The welcome at the airport was of course arranged by the joint protocol team of the Palace and regional government, but Nisa made sure the atmosphere stayed relaxed. There was pounding Gendang Beleq music welcoming them, making Caroline immediately nod along to the rhythm.
“Now this is music that raises the spirit! Local version clubbing!” she exclaimed.

The journey to their lodging in Lombok's southern coastal area (a somewhat remote location chosen for maximum privacy) presented a view different from Java. Barren yet exotic limestone hills blended with a stunning blue coastline. Residents' houses with characteristic Sasak rice barns looked unique along the road.
“This place feels… wilder? More raw?” Sharon commented, trying to find the right word.
“Correct, Sharon. Lombok has its own charm. Calmer than Bali, but its nature is no less fierce,” Nisa answered while pointing toward the white sand beach visible in the distance.

Their lodging wasn't a grand five-star hotel, but a very beautiful private villa complex, located in a hidden small bay with direct access to a quiet white sand beach. Each villa had a small private pool and a terrace facing directly onto the sea. Truly the definition of earthly paradise for relaxation.

“OH MY GOD! INSANE! DID WE JUST WALK INTO A TOURISM BROCHURE?!” Andrea shrieked seeing the view from her villa terrace. An expanse of clean white sand, clear blue-green gradation seawater, and swaying coconut palms. She immediately dropped her handbag and jogged toward the shoreline, ignoring Alex's shout reminding her to put on sunblock first.

Caroline and Sharon were no less enchanted. They immediately took out their respective phones, busy capturing every corner of that private beach's beauty. Jim? He found a large coral rock at the beach edge and immediately sat on it, gazing at the open sea with a contemplative stare. Is this coral rock a physical manifestation of wave uncertainty, or merely a geological marker of the boundary between land and sea? Who knows what else was in his mind this time.

Nisa and Reza only smiled seeing the happiness of their 'foster children' this month. “Seems like they feel at home here, Mas,” Nisa whispered. Reza nodded, “Who wouldn't feel at home in a paradise like this, Sa? You also look more relaxed.” Nisa did feel the burden on her shoulders lift slightly as soon as she breathed in Lombok's sea air.

That day was spent in total relaxation. Swimming in the calm sea, sunbathing (this time Caroline had been reminded repeatedly by Alex to wear sunblock), reading a book in a hammock strung between two coconut trees, or simply sitting on the terrace enjoying the sea breeze. No packed schedule, no official visits. Only quality time to enjoy nature's beauty and recharge energy.

That afternoon, when stomachs began growling and energy had recovered, Nisa had another “brilliant” idea. “How about tonight we cook dinner ourselves? Try Lombok's most famous specialty recipe: Ayam Taliwang!”

The Corrs, who all this time had mostly been culinary enjoyers, looked interested yet slightly apprehensive. “Cooking? Ayam Taliwang? That's the one that's supposedly very spicy, right?” Andrea asked hesitantly.

“Relax, we can adjust the spice level,” Nisa said convincingly. “I already asked Bu Fatimah, the local cook here, to prepare all the ingredients and seasonings. We just need to mix and grill them. Fun, right?”

So, the open kitchen in the villa's main area was transformed into a sudden cooking battlefield. Bu Fatimah, a Sasak woman generous with smiles, had prepared young free-range chickens already cleaned, a large mortar containing tempting red seasoning (chili, shallots, garlic, kencur, shrimp paste, palm sugar), and coconut shell charcoal ready to burn.
“Alright, The Corrs! Time to show your hidden talents in the kitchen! You can do it!” Reza exclaimed enthusiastically, acting as impromptu MC.

First task: grinding the seasoning to make it finer and more absorbed. Jim, with his researcher's soul, tried grinding with precise movements like pounding samples in a laboratory. The result? The seasoning jumped out of the mortar more than it got ground fine. Sharon, with her hand strength as a violinist, ground with full force until the mortar nearly broke. Caroline tried grinding while singing a rock song, making the grinding rhythm irregular. Andrea? She gave up after two minutes, complaining her hand was sore and it smelled of shrimp paste.
“Alright, alright, let Bu Fatimah finish the grinding part,” Nisa said while laughing at that chaos.

Second task: coating the chicken with the ground seasoning. This was the most fun part (and the messiest). Andrea, slightly disgusted holding raw chicken, did it with her fingertips while grimacing. Caroline instead made that chicken like a canvas, painting it with seasoning using a cooking brush. Jim was busy analyzing why red-colored seasoning could make chicken taste spicy. Sharon was most serious, ensuring every inch of chicken was perfectly coated with seasoning.

Last and most crucial task: grilling the chicken over coconut shell charcoal. This is where the real disaster began. Reza tried giving instructions about keeping the fire from getting too big and turning the chicken periodically. But The Corrs, who were perhaps too enthusiastic or too hungry, had their own ideas.

Jim, whose task was tending the fire, was busy fanning the charcoal with a giant satay fan until the fire blazed fiercely like burning a forest. Andrea and Caroline, whose task was turning the chicken, mostly chatted and laughed, forgetting their noble duty. Sharon, trying to save the situation, accidentally knocked one of the chickens until it fell into the sand (fortunately not yet too cooked and could still be “saved” after being quickly washed).
The final result? Ayam Taliwang The Corrs style. Most of it was… pitch black. Burnt outside, but inside perhaps still somewhat raw. The smoke aroma was more dominant than the seasoning aroma.
“This… this is called Ayam Taliwang Smoked Charcoal Limited Edition,” Alex quipped seeing the work of those Irish “masterchefs.”
Bu Fatimah could only smile understandingly. Fortunately, she had wisely prepared several portions of original Ayam Taliwang cooked properly as backup.

Dinner at the beachside that night was accompanied by nonstop laughter as they tasted (or tried to taste) the burnt Ayam Taliwang of their own creation. Andrea even saved the most burnt piece, “For a souvenir! A display! Proof that I once tried cooking the world's most exotic (and most failed) food!”

Although the cooking event ended with a bit of burning, that night felt so warm and enjoyable. Togetherness, laughter, and new experience (though failed) — that was the most delicious seasoning. They learned that sometimes, a chaotic process actually produces the sweetest memories (or the most… bitterly burnt?).

As stars began scattering across Lombok's clear sky, Nisa felt grateful for that day full of relaxation and laughter. The second week of adventure had just begun, and she knew there was still much silliness and other wonders awaiting them on the next islands.
8: The ninth morning was welcomed with a different view. No longer the private beach in Lombok, but calm blue waters separating Lombok from the famous Gili trio. President Nisa and The Corrs' entourage boarded a prepared private speedboat, heading to Gili Meno, the middle island known as most peaceful and suitable for families (or, in this case, a VVIP entourage needing extra tranquility after the burnt chicken incident).

“So, on this island there really are no cars or motorcycles?” Sharon asked in amazement as their boat docked at Gili Meno's simple wooden pier. There were only a few cidomo (Lombok and Gili's characteristic horse carts) and bicycles seen passing on the sandy roads.

“Absolutely right, Sharon,” Nisa answered while getting off the boat, helped by an alert Presidential Security Force member. “Here transportation is only bicycle or walking. The air is clean, the atmosphere calm. Suitable for relaxation before we face the 'underwater terror' of snorkeling tomorrow.” Nisa winked toward Jim and Caroline, remembering their panic during their first snorkeling.

Their lodging in Gili Meno was a collection of beautiful beachside bungalows with modern Sasak architectural style. After putting down their things and enjoying a welcome juice (Andrea made sure first there was no strange spice mixture in it), that day's agenda was: relaxed cycling around the island.

Colorful bicycles were already prepared. Some equipped with front baskets, some tandem models (Nisa and Reza immediately chose this one), and also mountain bikes (which Alex immediately chose). The Corrs looked enthusiastic.

“Wow, it's been so long since I rode a bicycle!” Caroline exclaimed while trying to mount the sky-blue bicycle she chose. She wobbled slightly at first, making Andrea shout, “Careful, Car! Don't fall into the sea before we go snorkeling!”
“Relax, I'm a drum expert, my balance must be good!” Caroline replied confidently, then began pedaling with great spirit.

The group began moving along the island's shaded path, flanked by coconut trees and small stalls selling handicrafts. On one side, calm blue-green sea views, on the other side the island's peaceful village life. Nisa and Reza cycled relaxed in front, enjoying the togetherness moment. Sharon and Andrea pedaled slowly while chatting and occasionally stopping to take photos. Jim, of course, cycled at the very back, busier observing types of beach sand and questioning its existence than enjoying the view. Alex? He had already sped far ahead, perhaps looking for the best sunset photo spot.

Caroline, who was initially enthusiastic in front, somehow began falling behind. Perhaps because she was too engrossed enjoying the view, or perhaps because she saw a beautifully colored butterfly and tried to follow it. Without realizing, when the main group turned right along the beach, Caroline instead went straight into a smaller path toward the island's middle.
“Where's Caroline?” Nisa asked when she realized The Corrs' youngest sibling wasn't behind them when they stopped briefly to drink young coconut water.
Andrea and Sharon looked at each other. “She was behind me earlier,” Andrea said. “Maybe she stopped briefly for a photo?”

They waited a few minutes, but Caroline didn't appear. Worry began creeping through Nisa and Reza. Alex, who had returned, also joined the search. Presidential Security Force members spread around the group began communicating via earpiece.
“Relax, maybe she just took a slightly wrong turn,” Reza said trying to calm Nisa and the other Corrs who were beginning to be anxious. “This island is small. Impossible to get lost far.”

Meanwhile, in the quieter middle part of Gili Meno island filled with coconut groves and bushes, Caroline Corr began realizing she was… alone. The path she followed grew increasingly small and grassy. The beautiful butterfly earlier had gone who knows where. The sound of crashing waves was replaced by the sound of bleating goats.
“Hello? Nisa? Reza? Andrea? Jim?” she called, her voice slightly trembling. No answer. Only the sound of goats growing louder.

She pedaled her bicycle faster, trying to find the way back to the beach. But that path branched out, making her increasingly confused. She saw several simple residents' houses, but she hesitated to ask because of the language barrier. Finally, she arrived at an open field that turned out to be… a goat grazing area! Dozens of goats of various sizes stared at her with innocent gazes (or perhaps suspicious?). A large male goat with curved horns even began walking toward her.

“Oh my Goood! Goats! Lots of goats! They want to attack me!” Caroline shrieked, immediately braking her bicycle suddenly, nearly falling. She remembered horror stories about mountain goats that like to ram in Ireland.

She tried to turn her bicycle around, but the path back was already blocked by a herd of curious goats. She was trapped! In the middle of a nowhere island (according to her), surrounded by a goat army! This was truly “Caroline's Great Escape” that wasn't cool at all!
On the other side of the island, Nisa, Reza, the other Corrs, Alex, and several Presidential Security Force members had begun panicking searching for Caroline. They spread out along the paths.
“What if she was kidnapped?!” Andrea exclaimed hysterically. “Maybe the kidnapper rode a cidomo!”
“Andrea, calm down. Who would want to kidnap Caroline on an island this small?” Sharon said trying to be logical, though she herself was also anxious.
“Maybe… maybe the aliens from Jim's painting yesterday?” Alex quipped, immediately rewarded with a sharp stare from Nisa.
That's when one of the Presidential Security Force members searching toward the island's middle heard a familiar high-pitched scream, interspersed with the sound of bleating goats.
“HEEEELP! THERE'S A GOAT THAT WANTS TO BE KING OF THE JUNGLE! HELP MEEEEE!”

That officer immediately contacted Nisa via earpiece. “Madam President, permission to report, Miss Caroline's position has likely been found. A scream for help was heard from the direction of the goat grazing field in the island's middle.”
Nisa took a relieved breath, but also shook her head with amusement. “Goat pen? What is she doing there?”

The group immediately headed to the location. And sure enough, they found Caroline standing on her bicycle saddle (however she managed it), surrounded by dozens of goats staring at her full of curiosity. Caroline's face was pale, her hair messy, but she was still trying to shoo those goats with dramatic hand waves.
“GO AWAY YOU EVIL GOATS! DON'T EAT ME!” she shouted.
Alex was the first unable to hold back laughter. “Goodness, Auntie Caroline! Those are goats, not lions! They're just curious about you!”

Seeing the rescue group arrive, Caroline immediately leaped down from her bicycle (and nearly fell again) then ran to hug Andrea. “I thought I would end up as the goat king's meal!” she sobbed dramatically.
The goat herders who turned out to be nearby could only smile with amusement seeing that foreign tourist's behavior. Nisa and Reza approached Caroline, making sure she was alright.
“Next time, Caroline,” Nisa said gently but firmly, “when cycling, don't chase butterflies. And remember, goats here are more interested in grass than in international drummers.”

The “Bicycle Gone Astray to the Goat Pen” incident became that day's most sensational story. That night, during grilled fish dinner at the beachside, Caroline was still slightly traumatized hearing goat sounds from a distance. But at least, she had an exciting (and slightly embarrassing) adventure story to bring home to Ireland. And Alex? Of course he had gotten enough material for the newest episode of his “President Nisa & The Corrs Go Nusantara” vlog.

The ninth day closed with relieved laughter and a promise from Caroline never again to separate from the group while cycling. Tomorrow, a new challenge awaits: conquering (or being conquered by?) Gili Air's underwater world! Will Jim meet the 'piranha' Nemo again?
9: Day 10: “Jim vs Nemo Fish: The Paranoid Snorkeling Episode with a Duck Float” — Gili Air's Underwater Terror

The tenth day marked a new adventure at the third Gili they would visit: Gili Air. After a relaxed breakfast at the Gili Meno bungalow (Caroline made sure there were no goat sounds nearby before daring to leave her room), the group again boarded a speedboat for the short journey to Gili Air. This island felt slightly busier compared to Meno, with more stylish beach cafes and a livelier atmosphere, yet still maintaining the charm of a small island without cars.

“Now, Gili Air is famous for its good and relatively calm snorkeling spots, suitable for beginners,” Nisa explained as they walked toward the beach area where snorkeling equipment was already prepared. She deliberately glanced toward Jim and Caroline when saying the words “calm” and “beginners,” remembering their previous underwater drama.
Caroline looked more confident this time. “Relax, Nisa! I'm mentally prepared! Yesterday I was just startled by seaweed that looked like a snake,” she said optimistically.
But Jim? His face had already begun to pale just from seeing the row of masks and snorkels. The shadow of the 'piranha' Nemo from the first snorkeling seemed to still haunt him.

“Do… do we really have to do this again?” he asked Reza in a slightly trembling voice. “I mean, isn't the sea's beauty more majestic if enjoyed from a distance, from a boat for instance? Letting its ecosystem not be disturbed by our presence… or vice versa?”

Reza patted Jim's shoulder. “Goodness, Jim. This is Gili Air, not the Bermuda Triangle. The fish are friendly. And look,” Reza pointed to the pile of floats, “we have a special 'safety device' for you this time.”
Among the standard orange floats was tucked one shaped like… a giant yellow duck with sunglasses. That was clearly Alex's idea.
Jim's face grew paler. “I… have to use… that duck?”
“Just think of it as your personal underwater vehicle, Om Jim! Guaranteed anti-sinking and anti-piranha! Anti-mini-electric-shock from Nemo too!” Alex exclaimed while holding back laughter.

With persuasion (and a bit of gentle coercion) from Nisa and the others, Jim finally agreed to join the snorkeling, but with conditions: he'd wear that duck float, and he'd stay near Reza or a Presidential Security Force member at all times.

So began the most absurd sight in Gili Air's waters that day: the Indonesian President's entourage and Irish rock stars preparing to snorkel, with one of its members, a skilled guitarist-philosopher-songwriter, floating awkwardly atop a giant yellow duck float looking cool with its sunglasses.

As soon as they began putting their heads into the water, Gili Air's beautiful underwater world immediately welcomed them. Colorful coral reefs, gently swaying sea anemones, and small tropical fish moving about peacefully. Sharon and Andrea were immediately enchanted, swimming slowly while pointing at the beauty below them. Caroline, this time truly enjoying it, even tried swimming closer to a large green turtle busy eating seaweed (fortunately that turtle was indifferent).
Nisa and Reza swam side by side, enjoying that calm moment. Alex was busy with his underwater camera, trying to get the best photo of The Corrs' mermaid (or duck) version.
But Jim? He floated stiffly atop his duck, his head only occasionally entering the water with hesitant movements. Every time a fish passed near him, he would immediately lift his head in panic.
“Reza! Reza! Just now… I saw something orange-white striped! So fast! That must be a mini barracuda species with high-level camouflage ability!” he exclaimed with ragged breath.
Reza, swimming near him, tried to calm him. “Jim, that was a clownfish. Nemo. Remember the Finding Nemo film? He isn't dangerous.”

“Not dangerous, you say?!” Jim replied in disbelief, his eyes bulging behind his mask. “In that film his father had to cross half an ocean to save him! There must be a reason why he was kidnapped! He must have some kind of… secret weapon! Maybe a mini electric shock, or neurotoxin in his fins!”
Nisa, hearing that conversation from nearby, couldn't hold back laughter inside her mask. Jim's conspiracy theories truly knew no bounds, even reaching into the clownfish world.
“Om Jim, Nemo is nice!” Alex shouted from a distance. “He just wants to say 'hello' maybe!”
“Hello by swimming zigzag at lightning speed like that?! That's clearly a tactic to deceive the enemy before they attack vital points!” Jim retorted, still certain of his theory.

For nearly the next hour, Jim's snorkeling session was mostly filled with restrained panicked shouts every time he saw a brightly colored fish (“That one! The blue one! Must be a Dory species with amnesia but deadly bite!”), or a somewhat large fish (“That must be a disguised shark! I read on the internet, there are sharks that can disguise themselves as ordinary fish!”), or even a starfish (“He's just still, but his stare is threatening! Maybe he's planning a coordinated attack!”). His duck float became a silent witness to the “underwater terror” experienced by Jim Corr at Gili Air.

Meanwhile, the other Corrs members were actually enjoying it greatly. Andrea even managed to overcome her slight fear and swam further, admiring the beautiful coral garden. Sharon looked so peaceful floating while observing small fish. Caroline even managed to “race” swimming with a triggerfish (and lost decisively).

When the snorkeling session finally finished and they returned to the beach, Jim immediately removed his mask and snorkel with a relieved breath. He stared at his duck float with a gaze mixing gratitude and slight resentment.

“Okay,” he said while drying himself with a towel. “I admit, the view was indeed… quite interesting from an underwater aesthetic viewpoint. But the level of alertness needed to survive among those deceit-filled creatures truly drains mental energy.”
Andrea patted her brother's shoulder. “Enough, Jim. What matters is you survived the attack of Nemo and Dory. Maybe next time we just bring an aquarium to your hotel room?”

That day closed with a relaxed lunch at one of Gili Air's beachside cafes, with the main menu being a fresh seafood platter (Jim made sure first there was no clownfish or Dory fish on his plate). They shared stories about their respective snorkeling experiences, which of course were dominated by Jim's heroic panic saga atop his duck float.

As afternoon approached, they returned to Lombok, leaving Gili Air with a million memories (and several new underwater conspiracy theories from Jim). Nisa felt relieved because this second snorkeling mission, though still colored by Jim's drama, was overall more successful than the first. At least no one was hysterical about seaweed again.

Tomorrow, a new adventure awaits in Flores. Will Jim be calmer facing komodo dragons (from afar)? Or will he instead have a new theory about komodo dragons' relationship with aliens? Only time will tell!
10: Labuan Bajo's morning sun welcomed the group with friendly warmth as they enjoyed breakfast on the gently swaying deck of the pinisi ship. Andrea's komodo trauma had subsided slightly (though she still occasionally glanced warily toward the nearest land), and Jim seemed to have moved on from komodo ancient DNA theory to a new topic: the geological formation of karst islands around Flores.

“Our agenda today is a bit different,” Nisa announced while sipping her morning Flores coffee. “We'll leave the sea's beauty for a moment and explore Flores's land wonders. We'll visit Batu Cermin Cave!”
“Cave? Mirror Stone?” Caroline repeated, her eyebrow raised. “Cool! Is there a magic mirror inside like in the Snow White story?”

Nisa laughed a little. “Not a magic mirror, Caroline. But they say the stone walls inside this cave can reflect sunlight like a mirror when hit by rays at certain times. Besides that, this cave also has beautiful stalactites and stalagmites, and of course… the cave's native residents.”
“Native residents?” Andrea asked suspiciously. “You mean… giant spiders? Pythons? Or… mini komodo versions living in caves?”
“More like… bats,” Reza answered casually, which immediately made Andrea's and Caroline's faces change slightly.
“Bats?! Vampire bats?! For God's sake!” Andrea shrieked.
“Not vampires, Andrea,” Nisa calmed her. “Ordinary bats, fruit or insect eaters. They're not dangerous, just… maybe a bit noisy and their aroma is distinctive.”

The journey to Batu Cermin Cave from Labuan Bajo port wasn't too far. This cave was located in the middle of dry limestone hills. Upon arriving at the fairly large cave mouth, cold damp air was immediately felt contrasting with the hot outside air. Several local guides were already waiting, carrying flashlights and safety helmets.
“Okay, everyone wear helmets,” Nisa instructed. “Inside it's somewhat dark and the ceiling is sometimes low.”

The Corrs wore their helmets in their respective styles. Jim's helmet was slightly too big, making him look like a mad scientist ready to conduct a dangerous experiment. Andrea's helmet was decorated with pink flower stickers (who knows where she got them). Caroline wore hers slightly tilted rockstar-style. Sharon's helmet fit best and neatest.

Entering the cave, the atmosphere immediately changed drastically. Dark, damp, with the sound of dripping water echoing faintly. Flashlight beams spotlighted strange and astonishing limestone formations. There were stalactites hanging from the ceiling like giant stone curtains, stalagmites growing from the cave floor like ancient mushrooms. In some parts, the stone walls looked to glisten when hit by flashlight, reflecting light like thousands of small crystals — this was perhaps the origin of the name Batu Cermin (Mirror Stone).
“Wow, this is like entering the earth's belly!” Sharon whispered in amazement, her voice echoing softly in the cave corridor.

Jim immediately busied himself observing the rock structure. “These calcite formations must have formed over thousands, maybe even millions of years. I want to know what the stalactite growth rate per century is in this cave? Is there a speed anomaly caused by geological resonance?” he asked the local guide, who could only smile in confusion.
Andrea walked at the very back, gripping Alex's arm tightly, her eyes warily observing the cave ceiling. “Are the bats asleep? Oh no! Don't let one fall on my head!”

When they arrived at a fairly large cave chamber with a high ceiling, the guide explained that the acoustics in this room were very good. “Sometimes when choir groups come here, they like to try singing in this room; their voices can echo so beautifully,” said the guide.

Hearing the words “good acoustics” and “singing,” Caroline's eyes immediately sparkled. Her entertainer's soul was called. Without waiting for anyone's approval, she stepped forward to the room's center, took a deep breath, then…
“DOOOOO…..!!!”
