22: The twenty-seventh day, also their last day in the enchanting Banda Islands, began with an extraordinarily calm atmosphere. After a breakfast of fried bananas sprinkled with cinnamon and nutmeg (Caroline made sure this wasn't leftover from her 'perfume' yesterday), Nisa had an idea to use the bright morning and spectacular view for one last relaxation session.

“How about we try meditating again this morning?” Nisa proposed as they relaxed on the guesthouse terrace, gazing across the sea where Banda Volcano stood sturdy, its peak occasionally puffing thin white smoke into the bright blue sky. “The view is very supportive for seeking inner tranquility.”
The Corrs' reactions were varied. Sharon looked agreeable. Jim nodded slowly, perhaps seeing this as a chance to 'communicate' more deeply with the island's volcanic energy.
Only Andrea looked slightly hesitant. “Meditation again? Facing an active volcano? Nisa, is this safe? What if he suddenly coughs louder?”
“Relax, Andrea,” Reza calmed her while smiling. “This Banda Volcano is considered 'friendly.' Just think of that thin smoke as the breath of a sleeping mountain.”

They looked for the perfect spot: on one of Belgica Fort's deserted bastions. From that old fort's height, Banda Volcano's view felt closer, more personal, yet still safe. They sat cross-legged facing directly toward that iconic volcano.
Sea breeze blew gently carrying the aroma of salt and spice. Nisa guided with simple instructions.

“Let us close our eyes,” Nisa began in a calm voice. “Feel the warmth of the morning sun… Listen to nature's sounds… And feel the presence of Banda Volcano before us. Not as a threat, but as part of this extraordinary beauty and power of nature.”

They all tried to dissolve into meditation. Jim? His eyes were closed, but his forehead slightly furrowed, perhaps trying to 'absorb' volcanic energy or thinking about the chemical composition of the smoke coming from the mountain's peak.
But Andrea? She couldn't fully close her eyes. She kept peeking toward Banda Volcano. That thin white smoke kept puffing, its shape always changing blown by wind.

Andrea's mind began to wander. That smoke… why does its direction keep going right? Can't it go left? She remembered science fiction films about controlling natural elements. Nisa said we have to merge with nature… if I truly focus, could I… control the smoke?

That idea began feeling increasingly interesting to Andrea. She closed her eyes tightly, ignoring Nisa's instructions. She began visualizing that white smoke inside her head. Okay, smoke, listen to me, Andrea thought with full concentration. I command you… move… to the left! Just a liiiittle to the left!
She furrowed her brow deeply, her lips slightly moving without sound. She even unconsciously moved her index finger slightly to the left, as if giving a command.
Alex, sitting not far from Andrea and pretending to meditate (when actually observing The Corrs' behavior for his vlog material), saw Andrea's strange movement. He held back laughter.
Andrea opened her eyes slightly, peeking toward the mountain. Its smoke? Still moving casually to the right, not affected at all by Andrea's 'mind power.'
Hmm, maybe not focused enough, Andrea thought. Or maybe I should try something easier first. Okay, smoke, now… stop puffing just for a moment! Still! Freeze!
She closed her eyes again, her concentration growing stronger. Her forehead furrowed more. Her hand slightly clenched. She held her breath.

Beside her, Caroline who was beginning to get bored meditating, opened her eyes and saw Andrea's strange expression. She nudged Sharon's arm gently. “Psst, look at Andrea. Her face is so tense like she's about to lift a barbell.” Sharon glanced briefly and held back a smile.
Suddenly, the smoke puff from Banda Volcano's peak looked slightly thicker and its shape changed. Andrea, who happened to open her eyes at that moment, immediately gasped.
It worked! she thought joyfully. The smoke changed shape! My mind power is working!
She grew more enthusiastic. Okay, now try making a heart shape! Come on, smoke, form a heart! Heart shape!

Of course, that volcanic smoke remained volcanic smoke. It kept puffing and moving randomly following wind direction, not caring at all about Andrea's desire to form a heart. After several minutes of trying to 'control' the smoke without result (other than making her forehead ache more from furrowing), Andrea finally gave up.
Well, maybe my mind power isn't trained enough yet, she thought, slightly disappointed. Or maybe volcanic smoke in Indonesia is too 'stubborn,' unlike chimney smoke in films.

That morning's meditation session ended with Nisa feeling fresher, Reza peaceful, Sharon calm, Jim perhaps having finished mapping the volcanic energy field in his mind, and Andrea keeping a secret about the 'failure' of her smoke control mission.
As they walked back, Alex playfully asked Andrea, “Auntie Andrea, why was your face so serious during meditation earlier? Like you were thinking about becoming a villain in an X-Men film.”
Andrea immediately became flustered. “Eh? Oh, no… I was just… deeply absorbing Nisa's instruction to merge with nature!” she deflected quickly.

Nisa, who heard that conversation, only smiled meaningfully. She had a hunch about what Andrea was actually thinking during meditation earlier. This Irish rock star always had something up her sleeve.

The last day in Banda Neira closed with a feeling of peace, full stomachs, and new spirit. They were slightly sad having to leave this spice island. But the most anticipated final adventure was already waiting: Raja Ampat! Hidden paradise at Indonesia's eastern tip.
Chapter 28 (Day 28): “Super Private Raja Ampat: Jim Lectures Colorful Fish About the Multiverse” — Peak of Relaxation

Leaving Banda Neira with the aroma of nutmeg and memories of meditation (plus Andrea's totally failed mountain smoke control effort) felt like closing an enchanting history book. The next journey was toward the hidden crown at Indonesia's eastern tip, a name always echoing in the ears of divers and lovers of maritime beauty: Raja Ampat, West Papua.

The journey here required extra effort. A flight from Ambon to Sorong, then continued with transfer using a luxury private yacht already waiting, carrying them sailing into the world's most iconic karst archipelago. As soon as they entered Raja Ampat waters, the atmosphere immediately felt different. Its sea was calmer, its color a turquoise blue gradation almost unreal, and small uniquely shaped limestone islands towered from the sea surface like giant green mushrooms. This wasn't merely beautiful, this was magical.

“Okay, I'm officially out of words,” said Sharon, usually the most poetic, standing on the yacht's front deck staring at the Piaynemo island cluster in the distance. “This… this exceeds all my expectations about tropical paradise.”

Andrea, who had momentarily forgotten her komodo and bat phobias, was now busy taking selfies with those karst islands as background. “No Instagram filter can beat the real view!” she exclaimed in amazement.

Caroline had already put on a chill reggae music playlist on her portable speaker. Alex, of course, had flown his drone again, this time with special permission to capture Raja Ampat's beauty from the air (and promising not to disturb Nisa-Reza's romantic moments again).

Nisa and Reza themselves looked most relaxed during this journey. Raja Ampat was indeed deliberately chosen by Nisa as the closing destination, as the “Peak of Relaxation.” The luxury yacht they rented was equipped with every facility.

They anchored in a very private hidden lagoon, surrounded by small uninhabited karst islands. Its water was so clear that the shallow seabed full of coral reefs and colorful fish was clearly visible from atop the boat.

That day was truly spent for total relaxation. Some swam leisurely in the calm lagoon, some did light snorkeling (this time Jim looked to enjoy it more, perhaps because the fish were more exotic and he hadn't had a chance to theorize about them), some simply sunbathed on the boat deck while reading a book. Nisa even managed to try stand-up paddle board again, and this time she didn't fall!

That afternoon, while relaxing on the yacht's back deck, several group members playfully threw leftover lunch bread crumbs into the water. Instantly, the water surface around the boat became busy with a swarm of colorful small reef fish — bright blue, lemon yellow, orange with white stripes, metallic purple — competing for food. That sight was so beautiful and entertaining.
Andrea and Caroline were most enthusiastic, laughing with amusement watching those fish compete. Nisa and Reza enjoyed that view while drinking warm tea.

But Jim Corr? He didn't join in throwing bread. He stood at the deck's edge, staring at that crowd of colorful fish with a very… intense gaze. Then, he cleared his throat softly, and began 'lecturing' those fish in a serious tone.

“O aquatic creatures inhabiting the coral reef,” Jim began his 'lecture,' making the others immediately turn toward him while holding back smiles. “You might think that this reality you inhabit… is the only reality that exists.”
Those fish of course didn't care, they were still busy competing for bread crumbs.

“But,” Jim continued, not at all disturbed by his 'audience's' indifference. “Have you ever contemplated the possibility of a multiverse? Parallel universes? Maybe in another reality, you aren't colorful fish swimming freely, but… who knows, maybe you're tax accountants in Dublin stressed about year-end reports?”
Alex could no longer hold back laughter and hurriedly recorded Om Jim's 'inter-dimensional lecture.' Andrea nudged Caroline, “Is he seriously talking to fish?”

“Maybe in another universe,” Jim continued his lecture to the fish still busy eating, “your blue color is actually green, and the taste of these bread crumbs is different. Maybe there's no kind-hearted President Nisa inviting an Irish band on vacation there, but an evil Klingon Emperor instead?”
A bright blue fish jumped slightly out of the water, perhaps because of competing for bread, but Jim considered it a sign of agreement.
“Ah, you understand my point, don't you, O blue fish? You feel the vibration of that multiverse truth!” Jim said while nodding with satisfaction.
Nisa finally couldn't take it anymore and burst out laughing, followed by Reza and the others (except Jim who was still serious).
“Jim, oh Jim,” Nisa said between her laughter. “I think those fish are more interested in bread than in your multiverse theory.”

Jim turned to Nisa, appearing slightly disappointed because his 'lecture' was interrupted. “What a shame. And I was just about to enter the discussion about Schrödinger's cat paradox, reef fish version.”

That day in Raja Ampat closed with a luxurious dinner atop the boat deck beneath a sprinkling of stars, as well as retelling how Jim Corr tried giving enlightenment about the multiverse to a school of hungry tropical fish.
The peak of relaxation in Raja Ampat was indeed achieved. Their bodies were pampered by natural beauty and the yacht's luxury, while their minds were 'pampered' by magical theories from Jim Corr.
23: The twenty-ninth morning came greeting in the most magical way in Raja Ampat. Long before the sun fully showed itself, soft color streaks — pink, orange, indigo — had already begun painting the eastern sky, reflected beautifully on the calm sea surface like a giant mirror. This was their last day enjoying the peak of relaxation in this hidden paradise.

The idea for sunrise yoga on the boat deck came from Sharon the night before. Nisa and Reza, who had already felt the benefits of total relaxation, welcomed it. Jim himself only nodded, perhaps already having a plan to analyze the sunrise light spectrum.

So, that morning, when the sky was still violet, their luxury yacht's upper deck had been transformed into a floating yoga studio. Mats were spread facing east. Sharon, appointed as impromptu 'honorary instructor,' guided a light stretching session and sun salutation.

“Let's begin with breathing,” Sharon's voice sounded gentle, merging with that morning's calm atmosphere. “Inhale deeply through the nose, feel Raja Ampat's fresh air filling your lungs… exhale slowly through the mouth, release all remaining tension…”

Nisa, who was usually always tense from state burdens, this time felt she could truly let go. Reza beside her looked so calm. Even Jim looked more 'normal,' only following the movements in his slightly stiff yet solemn way.

When the sun began truly peeking from behind the horizon, emitting its first golden rays, the atmosphere felt increasingly magical. Doing the warrior or triangle pose with a sunrise background in Raja Ampat was an experience hard to describe in words.

Perhaps inspired by that magical atmosphere and extraordinary relaxed feeling, Nisa felt like trying something slightly more challenging. When Sharon guided the Vrksasana pose (tree pose), a fairly difficult balance pose, Nisa did it quite well at first. But then, she saw a small stingray gliding gracefully in the clear water beneath the boat deck. Her attention was slightly diverted.
“Wow, look at that!” she whispered unconsciously to Reza, turning slightly.

And… her balance wavered. Her supporting foot slipped slightly on the mat that was perhaps somewhat damp from morning dew. She lost balance, her body beginning to tilt toward… the boat deck's railing!
“GOODNESS! NISA!” Reza shrieked reflexively, his hand immediately moving quickly trying to reach Nisa's arm.

Sharon, Andrea, and Caroline who saw that incident also let out restrained screams. Alex, who was recording the sunrise moment, immediately aimed his camera toward his mother. Jim could only gape, perhaps calculating his President's falling velocity vector.

For a fraction of a second that felt very long, Nisa felt her body would truly free-fall into that beautiful Raja Ampat sea. The image of the news headline “President Falls In During Morning Yoga in Raja Ampat” crossed her mind.

But fortunately, Reza's reflexes were very fast. He managed to grab Nisa's arm just in time, pulling her back to balance, though with a slight jerk that nearly made them both fall together. The Presidential Security Force guarding on the lower deck had also nearly leaped up.

Nisa's breath was ragged, her heart pounding hard, not only from nearly falling, but also from a mixture of shock, embarrassment, and amusement. She looked at Reza whose face was still slightly pale from worry.
“That was close…” Nisa whispered while trying to calm her heartbeat.

Then, seeing Reza's facial expression that was relieved but also slightly amused, and hearing Andrea and Caroline's giggling from behind, Nisa finally couldn't take it anymore. She burst out laughing, laughing at her own silliness.
“Hahahaha! Oh God! I almost became international headline news because of tree pose!” she laughed freely, inviting relieved laughter from the others.
“That's why, Madam President,” Reza said while helping Nisa stand upright, his tone teasing. “When doing yoga, focus on your breath, not on stingrays.”
“It's the fish's fault, why pass by exactly when I'm doing a difficult pose!” Nisa defended herself while laughing.

That “President Nearly Falls In” incident successfully became the most memorable (and most nerve-wracking) closing to their sunrise yoga session. After that, they all decided to just do Savasana pose (corpse pose), enjoying the morning sun's warmth without additional acrobatic risk.

Breakfast that morning was filled with jokes about Nisa's yoga pose that nearly ended with a 'morning swim.' Alex even already had a title for his vlog: “When the President Tried to Become a Tree But Nearly Became a Mermaid.”

Nisa could only surrender while laughing. At least, that incident became a reminder that however great a leader may be, she remains an ordinary human who can lose balance (literally and figuratively), and fortunately, she had a strong 'anchor' like Reza always ready to catch her when she nearly fell.
The twenty-ninth day in Raja Ampat, that peak of relaxation, turned out still not free from the touch of humor and unexpected incidents characteristic of their journey.
Chapter 30 (Day 30): “Best Tour Guide Certificate from The Corrs and the Promise of 'The Corrs Go Nusantara Part 2!'” — Sweet Farewell in Jakarta

The long flight from Sorong, West Papua, back toward the capital's heart, Jakarta, felt so different. The air inside the presidential plane cabin was filled more with comfortable silence, slight melancholy, and soft conversations reminiscing about the extraordinary adventure they had just passed through.
Thirty days exploring Indonesia. It felt like a long beautiful dream full of color (also full of laughter and slight panic).

“I can't believe it's been a month,” Sharon murmured while flipping through her sketchbook now full of drawings of landscapes, people, animals, and even… Nemo fish Jim's version. “It feels like just yesterday we choked on klepon at the Palace.”
“And I still can't forget that komodo's judgmental stare,” Andrea added while shuddering slightly, though now she could say it while laughing a little.
“I miss the sound of gamelan and Dayak drum beats,” Caroline said. “Maybe I should buy a mini gamelan for the studio later.”

Jim, who surprisingly wasn't reading a book, only stared at the clouds with a peaceful gaze. “This journey… gave so many new perspectives about the relationship between culture, nature, and human consciousness. I feel… inspired.” (Of course, there's still a philosophical element!)

Nisa and Reza held hands. Nisa felt extraordinary relief. This “super sudden month-long vacation” mission ran far more smoothly than she'd imagined (though there were several small incidents that nearly made her heart stop). The bond of friendship woven felt so sincere and strong.
As soon as they landed back in Jakarta, Nisa had already planned one closing event: a relaxed Farewell Brunch at a lush garden-themed restaurant in the South Jakarta area.

That brunch atmosphere was so warm and full of laughter. The long table was filled with a fusion of Western and Indonesian dishes The Corrs favored (there was fried rice again for Jim, chicken satay for Caroline, and rendang for Sharon who had become the Spice Queen). They shared stories about the funniest, most nerve-wracking, and most memorable moments.

“The funniest moment was definitely when Caroline was surrounded by goats in Gili Meno!” Alex exclaimed. “The most nerve-wracking for me is still when Jim nearly 'dialogued' with a male komodo!” Andrea said. “For me the most memorable was when we all tried singing a Batak song at that lapo,” Sharon said.
Nisa and Reza mostly listened while smiling, occasionally chiming in with stories from their perspective.

At the brunch event's end, when the atmosphere began feeling slightly emotional because farewell time was drawing closer, Andrea suddenly stood. “Ahem… attention everyone!” she said, imitating Nisa's style when giving a speech. “On behalf of The Corrs… we would like to give a special award.”
She signaled Caroline, who then produced a large gold-framed paper scroll (which looked slightly… crooked because it was perhaps made in a hurry).

“With pride and full gratitude (as well as slight pity for her patience),” Andrea continued reading the writing on that scroll, “we bestow: THE CERTIFICATE OF APPRECIATION FOR THE WORLD'S BEST, MOST PATIENT, AND MOST DARING TOUR GUIDE to… President of the Republic of Indonesia, Ibu Nisa Shabrina Farha!”

Below that writing were the signatures of all four Corrs members and several colorful ink thumbprints. There was also a small cartoon drawing of Nisa being chased by a grasshopper and nearly falling from a kayak.
Nisa burst out laughing receiving that 'certificate.' “Oh my goodness! You all always have something up your sleeves! Thank you so much!”
“That's proof that you succeeded in keeping us safe for a full month without anyone getting lost or eaten by komodos,” Sharon said while smiling.
“Also as a reminder,” Jim concluded, “that you have potential for a second career as an extreme adventure tour guide if someday you get bored being President.”

Besides that hilarious certificate, there was also a small farewell gift exchange session. Nisa gave each Corrs member a set of fine hand-drawn batik. Meanwhile The Corrs gave Nisa a distinctive Irish Aran wool scarf and several rare CDs of their albums.

“And this,” Andrea said while giving a small box to Nisa. “Don't open it now. Open it later when you really miss us.” (Its contents turned out to be a collection of candid photos of Nisa and Reza secretly taken by Caroline throughout the journey, including the photo of Nisa nearly falling in during yoga.)

Time to truly part at Soekarno-Hatta Airport. This time the atmosphere felt heavier. A month together had truly made them like family. There were tight embraces, there were a few tears (especially from Andrea and Nisa), there were promises to visit each other.
“Don't forget Indonesia, okay!” Nisa said while embracing Sharon. “Never,” Sharon answered. “We'll be back soon!”
“That's right!” Caroline chimed in. “We have to make The Corrs Go Nusantara Part 2: The Eastern Spice Route Boogaloo happen!”
“Or maybe 'The Corrs Search for the World's Most Delicious Durian'?” Andrea added.
Jim only smiled thinly. “I'll miss our philosophical discussions, Nisa, Reza. And also… the rawon.”

With a final wave, The Corrs entered the departure gate, bringing home heavier suitcases because of souvenirs (especially Andrea's bulk-bought Indomie) and hearts richer because of unforgettable experiences in this land of a thousand islands.

Nisa, Reza, and Alex stood frozen momentarily, watching the plane that would carry their Irish friends away. There was a loneliness suddenly felt, but also gratitude and happiness leaving its mark. That crazy and sudden month-long vacation had ended, but its story and friendship would be eternal.
24: A year passed since the 30-day adventure that shook (in the good and hilarious sense) Istana Negara and the corners of the Nusantara. President Nisa Farha and First Gentleman Reza Satria's lives slowly returned to the normal rhythm of statecraft, though “normal” their version now felt slightly different. There was a gold-framed crooked “World's Best (and Most Patient) Tour Guide” certificate displayed proudly (and with amusement) in the corner of Nisa's work room. The new frequency of harmony in their lives felt so real.

Meanwhile, in another part of the world, amid characteristic Irish drizzle, The Corrs didn't stay idle. The inspiration they gained from the month-long journey in Indonesia turned out to be more than merely a sweet promise. After months of shutting themselves in the studio (interspersed with several laughter-filled video calls with Nisa, Reza, and Alex for 'lyric consultation' or simply asking how they were), they finally released a long-awaited newest album.
The album's title? “Nusantara Whispers.”

And that album… was truly different. The Corrs' characteristic vocal harmony and Celtic touch were still there, but this time wrapped in arrangements rich with Indonesian sounds. There was faint Balinese gamelan sound, there was pounding Dayak drum rhythm, there was flowing Sundanese flute melody, there was even a sampling of the “klotok… klotok…” boat engine sound in one instrumental track.

Its lyrics were no less unique. Besides love songs, several songs clearly inspired by their journey were tucked in. There was a song titled “Ode to the Stingless Jellyfish” (a calming ambient song), there was “Sandalwood Horse Serenade” (an acoustic folk song), there was “My Arsik Heart” (a cheerful pop song about the most delicious food they'd ever tried), and of course, the flagship single whose music video caused an uproar: “Lost in the Floating Market (Where's My President?).”

That song's music video was truly a comedy masterpiece (perhaps unintentionally). That video showed The Corrs trying to interact at a floating market in Kalimantan. Amid the market's bustle, there was a scene where Nisa, trying to buy rambutan from atop a boat, suddenly had her boat carried by the current slightly away from the group. Nisa's panicked (but still trying to be graceful) expression as she tried to paddle her boat back using a fruit hook stick, while The Corrs waved frantically from another boat, became that video's peak of hilarity. Added to that with lyric translation subtitles sometimes deliberately made slightly over-the-top or contextually wrong by Alex, that music video successfully went viral worldwide, making people laugh while also becoming curious about Indonesia (and its President who turned out could get lost too).

Nisa and Reza watched that music video for the first time while relaxing in the pavilion. Initially Nisa protested slightly (“Alex! Why was that embarrassing scene included?!”), but finally she couldn't hold back laughter seeing her own facial expression. “Oh well,” she said resignedly. “Just consider this free tourism promotion. 'Visit Indonesia, where even the President can get lost in a floating market!'”

The album “Nusantara Whispers” was a great success. Their unique music, a blend between Celtic and Nusantara, was considered to bring a fresh wind. The Corrs even won several prestigious international music awards.
One night, Nisa, Reza, and Alex did a video call with The Corrs.
“Congratulations! Your album is so cool!” Nisa said sincerely. “I love the song 'My Arsik Heart' so much, I get hungry every time I hear it!”
“Thank you, Nisa!” Andrea answered cheerfully. “This is all thanks to inspiration from our journey! We wouldn't have been able to make it without you all!”
“And the music video!” Alex added while laughing. “Auntie Nisa's getting-lost moment is legendary!”
“Hey! That wasn't getting lost, that was… spontaneous exploration!” Nisa defended herself, which was met with everyone's laughter.
“Speaking of exploration,” Caroline said suddenly. “We're planning a world tour for this album next year. And we were thinking… maybe we could start the tour from… Indonesia again?”
Nisa's eyes gleamed. “Really? Wow, with pleasure!”
“But this time,” Andrea added with a mischievous smile, “besides concerts, we have a special mission.”
“What mission?” Reza asked curiously.
“The mission… 'The Corrs Search for the World's Most Delicious Durian!' We heard from Alex, that fruit smells like hell but tastes like heaven? We must prove it ourselves!”

Nisa and Reza looked at each other, then laughed. It seemed President Nisa and The Corrs' adventure truly wasn't really over. There would always be a reason to return, to laugh together, to create new harmony, whether in music, friendship, or in the search for the most delicious durian.

The frequency of harmony created during that month in the Nusantara kept echoing, not only in The Corrs' album, but also in all their hearts, becoming an eternal reminder of the beauty of difference, the power of laughter, and the miracle of an unexpected friendship crossing continents and cultures.
And who knows, maybe in “The Corrs Go Nusantara Part 2” later, it'll be President Nisa's turn to teach The Corrs how to eat durian without fainting? We'll just have to wait and see! 😉
THE END (for now 😉)!
